focus: What the 026/028/029 packets decided: command-shape rationale, rejected ideas, phase ordering
answeredQuestions: What did the 026/029 sk-code packets decide about what belongs in a setup check vs what stays out?

label: Placement precedent: a new doctor command /doctor:sk-code with one read-only target setup, per the /doctor:<owner> <target> grammar and one-per-owner rule; hub mode rejected (packetKind is workflow|surface, unroutable, 15+ files)

Rejected-idea catalogue X1-X11: no hub mode, no skill-advisor target (wrong owner), no parent-skill extension (contract corruption), no mutating repairs in a read-only route (route-validate enforces), no terminal add/remove script (needs judgment), no manifest minting in update --surfaces, no advisor surface-awareness (no failure)

Battery legs = executable form of the README Verify block: the six documented checks + provisioning precheck + CI-only derived-freshness gate + a probe asserting action:route because exit-0 could not fail

A setup check exists to make invisible/unactionable failures visible with named repairs: guard printing 'Re-mint: sk-code' with no command (F5), probe exit-0 on legacy stub (F7), CI-only gate missing from user battery (F16), fresh clone cannot reach green (F1-F3)

Phase ordering: P1 fixes the hand-followed path first (README before-you-start lines, guard message naming commands, named failure not stack); P2 builds the battery that prints those repair texts — the documented journey must be self-sufficient before a battery is worth running
Target name must cover the whole check surface: 'setup' chosen over 'surfaces' because the battery also covers provisioning

Route additions have a fixed recipe + validator: append _routes.yaml row, list in router and presentation, run route-validate.sh; every script enumerated in script_invocations; acceptance = pristine/stale/unprovisioned copy runs

026 shipped surface-priority semantics: user surface scaffolded ahead of native sk-code-opencode in tieBreak (check 5l fails a surface placed after it); OpenCode=native keep, Webflow/Obsidian=optional examples removable via 9-step recipe
Battery cost accepted at ~15s with one pass per leg; drift-guards is the leg that grows — a sk-git battery should time-budget its legs similarly
